text: 3. While Crusaders stormed Jerusalem in 1099, X recalculated the length of the solar year with astonishing accuracy. He advised sultans, debated theologians, and quietly mocked religious certainty in short, subversive verses. Though living in an age obsessed with salvation, he wrote about chance, doubt, and impermanence—ideas running counter to Crusader zeal. His works survived largely because Islamic scholars preserved them, only to be rediscovered by Europeans centuries later. While later known in a laterally different field, he was known as a mathematician originally.

4. During the desperate siege of Antioch, famine and despair stalked the Crusader army. X claimed Saint Andrew appeared to him in dreams, revealing the location of Y. An _________ ___________ was unearthed beneath a cathedral, sparking renewed faith and a surprise victory. Doubts followed. To prove divine favor, the visionary submitted to an ordeal by fire, walking between flames. He later died of burns, leaving history divided between miracle and manipulation.Which relic and claimant altered the First Crusade through belief rather than force?
